sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: T3 Code is an open-source app for running coding agents like Claude Code and Codex from one interface. It runs the agents on your machine and lets you follow and approve their work from the desktop, the web or your phone.
sixtySeconds.problem: Each coding agent has its own terminal or app, and you have to sit at your computer to approve its next step. T3 Code puts every agent in one fast interface with built-in git, and lets you continue a thread from anywhere.
whoFor: People who want to approve agent steps from their phone
Teams running agents on remote machines
Anyone wanting an open-source alternative to closed agent apps
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a free, MIT-licensed control plane that uses the agent subscriptions you already have. It does not provide models itself.
requirements: At least one coding agent installed and signed in, such as Claude Code or Codex CLI

overview: T3 Code does not resell tokens; it drives the agents you are already signed in to. It supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok Build, Antigravity, Kiro, Pi and any ACP agent, and you can change models in the middle of a thread or have one agent hand a task to another.
One server backs every client, so desktop, web and the iOS and Android apps show the same threads. You can run agents on any machine and connect over your local network, Tailscale or T3 Connect.

Each thread can work in its own git worktree; you review the diff and then commit, push and open a pull request with one button. The source is MIT licensed, but the T3 Code name and branding are trademarks, so forks must use their own branding.
